hyp-1.note: The title names variants; the chain starts at the genes, so the claims use the genes. Sign neg for RLS read from the title ('variants ... converge on disrupted synaptic differentiation and circadian sleep-wake circuitry'), the chain's required_for steps, and the mechanism ('its loss in mice disrupts circadian sleep/wake cycles'; 'aberrant synaptic differentiation ... lead to the sensory-motor symptoms ... of RLS'). The genes reach RLS only through unsigned association steps; the mechanistic branches end at processes, so claims 2 and 4 target those end nodes. Claim 5 is the title's convergence: MEIS1 variants 'converge on disrupted synaptic differentiation', the mechanism's 'shared pathophysiological pathway where aberrant synaptic differentiation ...', and the falsification block (perturbation: MEIS1 knockout; readout: synaptic differentiation; 'assess for defects in synaptic differentiation'). No chain step links MEIS1 to synaptic differentiation, so it has no route. PTPRD gets no circadian claim: only MEIS1 is tied to the circadian cycle in the mechanism, and the falsification's 'rhythmic activity' is network activity on multi-electrode arrays.

hyp-2.note: BTBD9 neg: 'when BTBD9 is disrupted by RLS-associated variants ... thereby precipitating RLS symptoms'. ACO1 has no claim: the mechanism gives both directions ('aberrant accumulation or dysfunction of ACO1'). The title's end node, 'neuronal iron deficiency', is not a chain node; the chain ends at RLS through the unsigned 'iron homeostasis' association.

findings.detail: The 'chain' is four separate edges from two genes: each gene has an unsigned association with RLS and a required_for edge to a process; neither process (circadian sleep/wake cycle, synaptic differentiation) is linked to RLS or to the other gene, so the convergence in the title has no step.

The mechanistic branches end at processes (circadian sleep/wake cycle, synaptic differentiation); only the unsigned GWAS association steps reach RLS, so process claims were added and the RLS claims have no route.

hyp-2.1 ends at RLS and hyp-2.2 starts again at BTBD9: the chain is a direct BTBD9-RLS association followed by a second, parallel path BTBD9-ACO1 -> iron homeostasis ~ RLS (hyp-2.2 to hyp-2.4 do connect), not one path.

The hypothesis's defining claim, that BTBD9 controls ACO1 turnover (a direction on ACO1 amount), is not a chain step; the chain has only 'BTBD9 binds ACO1' from a STRING edge (experimental 0.41), which carries no direction, so no arm can pass from BTBD9 to ACO1.

The mechanism says 'aberrant accumulation or dysfunction of ACO1 exacerbates cellular iron deficiency', which names both directions, so ACO1 gets no claim; the run's own UniProt citation (P21399) describes ACO1's mRNA-binding activity as promoted by iron deprivation, and the run does not say how more ACO1 would deepen iron deficiency.

Title and mechanism are about neuronal iron deficiency (a direction on iron amount), but the chain uses the undirected node 'iron homeostasis' with polarity unknown, so the direction the hypothesis depends on is lost before RLS.

All three gene-RLS steps are gene-level associations with polarity unknown, cited to GWAS rows that do give the risk allele's direction (rs113851554-T, rs34602324-G, rs10947738-A, all 'increase'); the run never says whether these alleles raise or lower gene function, so none of the gene claims can reach RLS.
required_for steps are cited to MGI 'abnormal X' annotations (abnormal circadian sleep/wake cycle, abnormal iron homeostasis), which give no direction; hyp-1.2 is left with no evidence.

BTBD9's association with RLS is cited partly to a Purkinje-cell Btbd9 knockout mouse with 'abnormal sleep behavior', a different phenotype from RLS; the mechanism restates it as 'disruption causes abnormal sleep behavior in mice' in support of an RLS gene.

The PTPRD function text the run cites ('Can bidirectionally induce pre- and post-synaptic differentiation of neurons') carries ECO:0000250 from mouse Q64487 (by similarity), but the mechanism states it as human PTPRD function.

The run left the CURIE empty for all three process nodes, although 'circadian sleep/wake cycle' is GO:0042745 exactly and 'iron homeostasis' is an exact synonym of GO:0006879; only 'synaptic differentiation' lacks a GO label or synonym.
The run marks hyp-2 support 'grounded', yet no citation addresses BTBD9-mediated ACO1 turnover, the claim in its title; confidence 'low' is fair.
The budget asks for min_hypotheses 3; the run returns two hypotheses and one abstention covering GLIPR1 and GABARAPL2.

The abstention for GLIPR1 and GABARAPL2 cites GWAS:GLIPR1:no-association, GWAS:GABARAPL2:no-association, AGR:MGI:1920940:MP:0002020 and AGR:MGI:1890602:MP:0011100, none of which is in sources.json, so its 'no GWAS association' claim cannot be checked; the curation format has no place for an abstention at all.

A GWAS row supports a gene-level association only through the Catalog's positional 'mapped gene'; the format cannot record that variant-to-gene step, and the allele's direction cannot be carried to the gene, so gene-level GWAS associations stay unsigned and never compose.

A null result for a gene (the abstention's 'no association with RLS') has no statement form: assoc direction 'none' means 'unsigned', not 'no association', and a null only enters as a refuting citation on a step the run made.

An MGI 'abnormal X' annotation of a mutant allele is the usual evidence that a gene is required for X, but the guide excludes it as no_direction; a rule that a knockout allele with 'abnormal X' supports 'required_for X' would need the allele type, which the Alliance text does not give.
An effect 'pos' on a homeostasis process (iron homeostasis) means 'takes part in', not 'raises'; it composes like an increase, though no amount is raised.

'synaptic differentiation' has no GO label or synonym (searched synaptic differentiation, presynaptic differentiation, synaptogenesis, synapse assembly, synapse organization, synapse maturation); grounded to GO:0007416 synapse assembly (synonym synaptogenesis), not a BLN term.

One STRING edge with combined score 0.45 (experimental 0.41) is curatedDb under the guide's 0.15 channel cut, so it alone makes 'BTBD9 binds ACO1' established (belief 4/5), the same weight as a curated UniProt assertion.
A hypothesis claim whose direction is stated as either-or ('accumulation or dysfunction of ACO1') cannot be recorded; the ACO1 claim is dropped and survives only in the note.

The falsification perturbs MEIS1 (knockout) and reads out synaptic differentiation, a link no chain step states and no citation supports (MEIS1's only mechanistic step goes to the circadian sleep/wake cycle); the convergence the title rests on is therefore uncited, yet hyp-1 is marked support 'grounded'.

The mechanism calls brain iron deficiency 'a central hallmark of RLS' (a disease feature) and has it 'precipitating RLS symptoms' (a cause), but the step's only citation, PMID:30363981, says 'the precise role that iron or other components of iron metabolism play in bringing about RLS is still a matter of debate'.

The end-node rule yields claims that are a single chain step restated (MEIS1 →+ circadian sleep/wake cycle is S2, PTPRD →+ synapse assembly is S4), so hyp-1's two 'arms' test nothing beyond those steps, while the claim that joins the branches (MEIS1 →+ synapse assembly) has no route.

audit.reason: The title's point is convergence ('Variants in MEIS1 and PTPRD converge on disrupted synaptic differentiation'), the mechanism names synaptic differentiation as the shared pathway, and the falsification block perturbs MEIS1 with readout synaptic differentiation. The curated claims only restated each gene's own chain step, so the convergence claim was never tested; recorded now, it has no route.

audit.after: a direct BTBD9-RLS association followed by a second, parallel path BTBD9-ACO1 -> iron homeostasis ~ RLS (hyp-2.2 to hyp-2.4 do connect), not one path
audit.reason: hyp-2.2 (ACO1), hyp-2.3 (ACO1 -> iron homeostasis) and hyp-2.4 (iron homeostasis -> RLS) link end to start; only the 2.1/2.2 junction breaks. 'Star at BTBD9' misdescribes it.
